observedFailures.mechanism: Cross-area continuation created a fresh server session and planned from compressed coverage/pattern metadata rather than retaining the complete preceding participant-answer context. A semantically answered construct could therefore be selected again when the metadata remained open or incomplete.
observedFailures.lesson: A dynamic interview needs continuity of participant-answer memory across measurement areas; compressed coverage state alone is not a substitute for the conversational evidence needed to suppress duplicate questions.

observedFailures.mechanism: The product exposed an internal topic-completion boundary as a participant action, requiring a redundant Continue interview click even though the next authorized system action was deterministic.
observedFailures.lesson: When the workflow has exactly one nonterminal next action, advance automatically. Preserve a continuously visible Finish/Pause affordance for participant control rather than inserting a redundant continue checkpoint.

observedFailures.mechanism: Information-gain/redundancy criteria existed only as generation instructions. The generated question itself did not pass a distinct pre-send admission boundary capable of rejecting a redundant, generic, low-discrimination, or questionnaire-for-its-own-sake prompt.
observedFailures.lesson: Before exposing another interview question, require an explicit admission check: name the missing discriminator, show how materially different plausible answers would change interpretation, and verify the substance has not already been answered.

observedFailures.mechanism: The always-available free-form textbox already handled explanatory feedback, while a separate 'Close — I’ll explain what needs changing' button merely routed to that same action. This leaked implementation-state distinctions into the participant UI.
observedFailures.lesson: Do not expose two controls for the same semantic action. Keep free-form chat for ordinary feedback; retain a separate exact-wording control only when it has a genuinely different contract—literal participant-authored wording recorded unchanged.
